newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says cen bank gold sales cannot reduce deficits.
newsitem.headline: EU says cen bank gold sales cannot reduce deficits.

text.p: Eurostat, the EU's statistical office, said on Monday that gold sales by national central banks could not be used to reduce budget deficits in line with Maastricht treaty criteria on membership of Economic and Monetary Union.
The ruling, however, did not suggest that outstanding public debt could not be reduced through the use of gold sales.

"Eurostat has decided that the sale of gold and the subsequent transfer of the proceeds from the sale to the general government should be treated as a financial transaction," a document from Eurostat said.
"This means that the proceeds from the sale cannot be recorded as a receipt reducing the deficit in the same way."
Eurostat included several other areas of financial accounting in its report.

In the case of zero coupon bonds, for example, the office has decided to treat the difference between the issue price and redemption price of a bond as interest, and to be recorded as interest paid when the bond matures.
There was no discussion of Italy's "Euro-tax", a controversial proposal by Rome to bring its deficit in line with the Maastricht treaty.
But it did address the treatment of fungible bonds, an area which is of concern to the Italian government as well.
On this issue, Eurostat said that the accrued coupon on such bonds should be "recorded as a short-term liability" and would not enter into a calculation of outstanding government debt.
